author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Pushed a follow-up commit on top of `69a1c530b`. @Bullo27 and @AnayGarodia are co-authors on it.

Two behaviour changes come from #1683 by @Bullo27:

- `--tifxyz-source` now reduces the source scale by the decimation applied: `src_scale * (decimated_cols - 1) / (source_cols - 1)` per axis. On the published `20231007101619-on-20260310170716-45.532um.tifxyz`, round-tripped with `--uv-downsample=4`, the 72 x 35 grid now gets 0.0125 (80 voxels per cell) instead of 0.05 (20). Measured spacing is 77.5 x 75.1 voxels. Without decimation it still writes 0.05.
- `mesh_units` no longer changes the scale. `20231007101619.obj` with `2000 7.91` wrote 0.00760764, 0.0157312 and now writes 0.0601765, 0.124434. That matches the measured 16.61 x 8.03 voxel spacing and the `2000 1.0` result.

The push also takes #1683's wording for the definition of `scale` in `tifxyz_format.md` and drops the two bullets there that contradicted it. It adds five e2e subcases (the previous binary fails 6 checks, the new one passes) and removes most of the code comments from the first commit. The description now includes these numbers and a Prior work section.

@Bullo27, @AnayGarodia, @olgaiv39: thank you for #1683, #1630 and #1391. All three got to these fixes before this PR, and the new commit takes #1683's source-scale and `mesh_units` handling and #1630's 2 x 2 refusal and hint removal directly.

Points raised on the earlier PRs that the first commit did not cover, and the new commit now addresses:

- On #1630, @Bullo27 found a normalised-UV mesh that fills 1 of the 4 corners of a 2 x 2 grid and slips past a zero-only check. @AnayGarodia then refused every 2 x 2 grid, since it is the clamped minimum and comes out degenerate whatever the user passes. The new commit does the same: exit 1, nothing written. A fully valid 30 x 30 window of the published tifxyz above, exported with `--normalize-uv` and converted at the default stretch, rasterized 1 of 4 points. `69a1c530b` wrote a 2 x 2 tifxyz with scale 1.0 and exited 0. Now it prints `Error: degenerate 2 x 2 output grid (1 of 4 points rasterized); refusing to write a tifxyz.` and exits 1.
- On #1630, @bruniss asked to stop recommending `--uv-to-obj` and just report the invalid output. The hint is gone. `--uv-to-obj` never changed the grid size, since the UV-metric grid is `ceil(uv_range * stretch_factor) + 1`. The default invocation on `20231007101619.obj` now prints the empty-grid error with no hint and exits 1.
- On #1391, @hendrikschilling asked for tests that vary `stretch_factor` and check the emitted grid. A new subcase runs stretch 20 and 80 and checks for a 21 x 21 and an 81 x 81 `x.tif`, with scale 0.05 and 0.2.

If anything else from your versions should come across, please say so.

> [Christos: I only found #1391, #1630 and #1683 after opening this PR. So I went back through their review threads and brought in the points that mine didn't cover yet. I reran the conversions on the published Scroll 1 data after the change, and I [looked at the new outputs / reviewed the follow-up diff] myself.

author: nerln
body:
Independent reproduction, same numbers on both commits: 449369 / 496584 valid points at stretch 800, and a 54 x 619 `vc_flatten` grid with 28059 valid points at stretch 200, from a binary built off this branch and run on a real published PHerc0125 segment.

I opened #1794 for the #1320 half before seeing this consolidation and have closed it in favour of this PR.

Setup: `z6336_w020_normuv.obj`, UVs normalised to [0,1], built from the actual geometry of a published PHerc0125 segment (declared scale 0.05, i.e. a 20-voxel step; measured spacing between adjacent grid points 20.8 voxels along u and 20.0 along v). `vc_obj2tifxyz`/`vc_flatten` built from this branch on macOS arm64 (LLVM/OpenBLAS, OpenCV 5), first at `69a1c530b` and again at `8b8537e45`. I had prepared local patches for #1319/#1320 and validated them on the same file; they are superseded by this PR.

Numbers from the `8b8537e45` binary, unchanged from `69a1c530b` on every case:

- Default args (no stretch factor): exit code 1, output directory not created. stderr, in full: `Error: no valid grid points were rasterized (grid 2 x 2); refusing to write an empty tifxyz.` then `Failed to create quad surface`. The `Hint:` line of the first commit is gone, as bruniss asked in #1630. Matches #1320.
- `stretch_factor=800, mesh_units=1.0`: grid 792 x 627, 449369 / 496584 valid points (90.49%).
- `stretch_factor=200, mesh_units=1.0`: grid 199 x 158, 28221 / 31442 valid points. `meta.json` scale `[0.0588083, 0.1824135]`; measured independently in Python (mean distance between adjacent valid grid points along u and v, 17.00 and 5.48 voxels, inverted) `[0.0588, 0.1825]`: written vs. measured differ by 0.00% and 0.05%, rounding only. Matches #1319.
- `vc_flatten` on that output: grid 54 x 619, 28059 valid points, instead of the 6 x 18 / 64-point collapse the old UV-derived scale produced.

No discrepancy: this confirms both fixes, on both commits, on data neither of us used to write the patches.

Two notes from the diff, not from running anything, and not asking to expand the PR: (1) the `--uv-non-metric` path is rewritten onto the same measured-spacing logic, but every subcase in `test_obj2tifxyz_e2e.cpp` still runs default UV-metric mode, so that branch stays untested; (2) the follow-up refuses *every* 2 x 2 output grid, including one where all four corners rasterize (`grid_size[0] <= 2 && grid_size[1] <= 2` fires regardless of `valid_count`), so a legitimately tiny or heavily decimated segment is refused like the degenerate 1-of-4 case; worth knowing. The `mesh_units` gap I saw on the first commit is closed by the new subcase and the numbers in your comment.

author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Thanks @nerln for the independent reproduction on a real PHerc0125 segment, on both commits, and for folding #1794 into this PR.

On your two notes:
1. Agreed, the `--uv-non-metric` path has no end-to-end subcase yet. I'm happy to add one here if the maintainers want it in this PR.
2. Refusing every 2 x 2 output grid is intentional. @bruniss asked for that in #1630, because a 2 x 2 grid from this tool almost always means a degenerate UV or scale input rather than a real, tiny segment.

author: hendrikschilling
body:
```
1. P2: Make the coordinate-unit contract explicit instead of silently ignoring mesh_units.
     In volume-cartographer/apps/src/vc_obj2tifxyz.cpp, the old mesh_units behavior was incorrect: it changed scale metadata without converting the stored coordinates. Removing that       
     multiplication is correct for OBJs already expressed in base voxels, but silently accepting an argument documented as “micrometers per OBJ unit” remains misleading.

     Support the two cases explicitly:

     --coords base-voxels                  # default: leave XYZ unchanged

     --coords physical
     --obj-um-per-unit <value>
     --voxel-size-um <scalar or x,y,z>

     For physical coordinates, convert vertices before rasterization:

     xyz_base = xyz_obj * obj_um_per_unit / voxel_size_um

     Then derive scale from the reciprocal of measured output-grid spacing in base voxels. Preserve the existing source-scale policy when --tifxyz-source is supplied, including its        
     decimation adjustment. Require positive, finite conversion parameters and reject contradictory options. Deprecate mesh_units; until explicit conversion exists, reject non-default     
     values with an explanatory error. Alternatively, keep this PR narrow and explicitly support only base-voxel OBJs.

  2. P2: Cover the changed --uv-non-metric path.
     volume-cartographer/core/test/test_obj2tifxyz_e2e.cpp currently exercises metric and source-scale modes only. Add a non-metric conversion test that reads the emitted XYZ arrays,      
     measures adjacent-point distances, and checks their reciprocals against the written scale. Include decimation. If coordinate conversion is added, test equivalent base-voxel and       
     physical-coordinate OBJs producing equivalent outputs.

  3. P3: Make the E2E process invocation portable.
     The new test concatenates unquoted paths into std::system() and splits PATH using :. Paths containing spaces fail, and Windows uses a different separator. Prefer an argument-list     
     process API, such as QProcess, using the executable path already supplied by CMake.


```

author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Thanks for the review. Three commits on top of `8b8537e45`, one per point, pushed to this branch.

**1. Coordinate-unit contract (P2)** — `30b330f83` takes the narrow route: the tool explicitly supports base-voxel OBJs only. `mesh_units` is deprecated; `1.0` is still accepted so existing invocations keep working, and any other value exits 1 before the OBJ is read, with nothing written:

```
Error: mesh_units 7.91 is not supported. vc_obj2tifxyz expects OBJ coordinates in
base voxels and writes them unchanged; it does not convert physical units. The
argument is deprecated and only its default 1.0 is accepted.
```

The help text states the same contract (`mesh_units: deprecated; must be 1.0. OBJ coordinates are expected in base voxels and are written unchanged; the tool does not convert physical units.`), each run logs `OBJ coordinates: base voxels (written unchanged)`, and the `800 1.0` example no longer advertises the argument. Nothing in the repo passes `mesh_units` (VC3D passes `--uv-downsample=20`, `render_ink.py` passes `--tifxyz-source`). The explicit conversion (`--coords physical` with `--obj-um-per-unit` and `--voxel-size-um`, converting vertices before rasterisation and keeping the `--tifxyz-source` policy) is left for a follow-up PR.

**2. `--uv-non-metric` coverage (P2)** — `2b60cf6f3` adds the subcase offered in the reply to @nerln. It converts the normalised 41 x 41 plane (10-voxel spacing) with `--uv-non-metric`, once plain and once with `--uv-downsample=2`, reads the emitted `x/y/z.tif`, averages the distance between adjacent valid grid points along each axis and checks the reciprocals against the written `scale` (2% tolerance). It also pins both runs to a 401 x 401 grid at scale 1.0: in non-metric mode the decimation only thins the preliminary grid the spacing is measured on, and the final grid is `round(spacing * stretch) + 1` from the compensated measurement either way (that sizing predates this PR), so a wrong compensation would change the grid even though the scale would still describe it.

**3. Portable process invocation (P3)** — `39bb6ae2e` starts the tool through `QProcess` with a `QStringList`; Qt6::Core is already required by the test build. The only binary lookup is `VC_OBJ2TIFXYZ_BIN`, which the ctest registration sets to `$<TARGET_FILE:vc_obj2tifxyz>`; the `PATH` split and the relative `build/bin` probes are gone. The temporary root is now `vc_obj2tifxyz e2e <n>`, so every subcase runs the tool on paths with spaces. A run that fails to start or exits abnormally is a test failure instead of a non-zero code that a negative subcase could mistake for the expected refusal.

**Evidence** (Linux, `ci-release-gcc` preset with `VC_TESTING=ON VC_RUN_E2E=ON`, at `2b60cf6f3`):

- `ctest -R obj2tifxyz --output-on-failure`: `test_obj2tifxyz_e2e` passed, 1/1 in 0.73 s. That runs all nine subcases: empty-grid refusal, 2 x 2 refusal, normalised-UV scale, stretch 20/80 grid sizes, decimation, `mesh_units` 1.0 accepted and 7.91 rejected, non-metric plain and decimated, source-scale with and without decimation.
- The same test executable pointed at a `vc_obj2tifxyz` built from `8b8537e45` fails exactly the three `mesh_units` checks (7.91 accepted, output directory created, no error text) and nothing else, so the non-metric, metric and source-scale subcases pass on both binaries and only the new rejection separates them.

AI-assisted (Claude Code), human-directed.

author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Please do take it, @nerln — thanks. Two things from this PR worth keeping aligned: the `mesh_units` error text now states the base-voxel contract, so `--coords base-voxels` should read as the documented default of the new flag; and `test_obj2tifxyz_e2e.cpp` already has the QProcess spawn helper and a temp root with spaces, so the equivalence subcase can drop straight in. I'll leave the follow-up to you.
